EMAMI LAB

Computational & Precision Ophthalmology
Imaging · Data Science · Precision Medicine
UC Davis Department of Ophthalmology & Vision Science

Personalized, data-driven care for inflammatory and retinal disease.

Our lab develops computational and precision ophthalmology approaches spanning advanced imaging biomarkers, EHR-based machine learning, clinical trial pipeline optimization, and translational clinical research to detect retinal disease earlier, predict outcomes, and personalize treatment.

Computational & Precision Ophthalmology
Research

Imaging Biomarkers for Uveitis

We develop noninvasive imaging approaches to characterize inflammation in uveitis, with the goal of creating more accessible and quantitative biomarkers for clinical care and research.

AI & EHR-Based Prediction

We use machine learning and clinical data to study disease activity, treatment response, and complication risk in uveitis.

Imaging & Multiomics in Neovascular AMD

We integrate longitudinal retinal imaging with molecular data to identify biomarkers of disease activity and treatment response in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

Clinical Trial Pipeline Optimization

We study how clinical trial workflows, resource allocation, and operational decision-making can be improved to make ophthalmic clinical research more efficient, scalable, and predictable.

Team

Parisa Emami, MD, MPH

Associate Professor of Ophthalmology · Director, Uveitis Division, UC Davis

Dr. Parisa Emami is a vitreoretinal surgeon, uveitis specialist, and physician-scientist at UC Davis. She directs the Computational and Precision Ophthalmology Lab, where her team develops approaches to improve the diagnosis, prediction, and treatment of retinal and inflammatory eye disease. Her research integrates advanced retinal imaging, artificial intelligence, clinical data science, and translational clinical research, and the lab’s work spans imaging biomarkers, EHR-based prediction, multimodal data integration, and methods to improve the efficiency and precision of clinical research. At UC Davis, she directs the Uveitis Division and leads a multidisciplinary clinical and research program focused on translating computational and biologic insights into practical tools for more individualized ophthalmic care.

New Grant

NIH/NEI R34 Awarded

The Emami Lab received a $483,000 NIH/NEI R34 award to develop and validate noninvasive multimodal imaging biomarkers for uveitis.

Now Hiring

We have an immediate Postdoctoral Scholar opening jointly with the LARA Lab at UC Davis.

We are seeking candidates with a PhD in Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, Medical Imaging, or a related field, with experience in machine learning, computer vision, medical imaging, or healthcare AI.

The position will focus on interdisciplinary work at the intersection of AI, ophthalmic imaging, and clinical data science.

If interested, please send your CV and a brief description of your research background to contact@emami-lab.com.
